ancestry_summary.statement_nl: Let [n choose k]_q denote the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient. Prove that for all integers n, k, l with 0 ≤ k, l ≤ n, if [n choose k]_q / [n choose l]_q is a polynomial in q, then that polynomial has only nonnegative coefficients.

payload.proof_nl: Work in the rational-function field in q. By definition, [n choose r]_q = (prod_{i=1}^r (1 - q^(n-r+i))) / (prod_{i=1}^r (1 - q^i)), and, replacing r by n-r, [n choose n-r]_q = (prod_{i=1}^{n-r} (1 - q^(r+i))) / (prod_{i=1}^{n-r} (1 - q^i)). Set A = prod_{i=1}^r (1 - q^(n-r+i)), B = prod_{i=1}^r (1 - q^i), C = prod_{i=1}^{n-r} (1 - q^i), and D = prod_{i=1}^{n-r} (1 - q^(r+i)). Then [n choose r]_q = A/B and [n choose n-r]_q = D/C. The factors in A are exactly (1 - q^t) for t = n-r+1, ..., n, while the factors in C are exactly (1 - q^t) for t = 1, ..., n-r. These two index sets are disjoint and their union is {1, ..., n}; hence, by commutativity of multiplication, A C = prod_{t=1}^n (1 - q^t). Similarly, the factors in D are exactly (1 - q^t) for t = r+1, ..., n, while the factors in B are exactly (1 - q^t) for t = 1, ..., r, so again the index sets are disjoint with union {1, ..., n}; hence D B = prod_{t=1}^n (1 - q^t). Therefore A C = D B. Now B and C are nonzero (each is a finite product of factors 1 - q^i, or an empty product equal to 1), so in the rational-function field we may divide by B C and obtain A/B = D/C. Thus [n choose r]_q = [n choose n-r]_q. This includes the boundary cases r = 0 and r = n, since the relevant empty product is 1.

payload.statement_nl: For integers n and r with 0 <= r <= n, define the Gaussian q-binomial coefficient by [n choose r]_q := prod_{i=1}^r (1 - q^(n-r+i)) / (1 - q^i), with the empty product equal to 1 when r = 0. Then [n choose r]_q = [n choose n-r]_q.

detailed_findings.finding: The proof is mathematically sound: AC and DB are each identified with the same full product over t=1,...,n, yielding A/B = D/C after division in the rational-function field.
Boundary cases r=0 and r=n are explicitly covered via the empty-product convention.

result_payload.reason: The proof correctly derives the standard symmetry identity for Gaussian q-binomial coefficients by writing both sides as ratios of complementary subproducts of ∏_{t=1}^n (1-q^t). The argument is complete, includes the empty-product boundary cases r=0 and r=n, and stays aligned with the lemma’s intended role of replacing indices by their complements.
